content.prompt: Put these turning points in order
content.instruction: Arrange them from earliest to latest.

options.label: Roman territory reaches its greatest extent
The last western emperor is removed
The empire passes to separate eastern and western rulers

content.prompt: Why is 476 CE an incomplete date for the end of Rome?

choices.label: The empire disappeared everywhere at the same moment.
It marks a western political change while Roman government continued in the east.
It was the year Augustus created the empire.
It was the year Rome reached its greatest extent.

content.prompt: Select the two regions that show Rome’s reach from northwest to east in 117 CE.
content.mapDescription: The shaded territory surrounds the Mediterranean. Its northwestern edge crosses the Channel beyond Gaul, while its far eastern edge reaches beyond Syria.

content.prompt: How did Rome change by 117 CE?
content.instruction: Write exactly two sentences: one on territory, one on what Augustus kept and controlled.

content.prompt: What mattered more to Rome's transformation: its size or its political conflicts?
content.instruction: Make a claim. Use three pieces of evidence. Address one complication.

rubric.label: Claim
rubric.description: Takes a clear position on size, political conflict, or a qualified relationship.

rubric.label: Evidence
rubric.description: Uses at least three accurate examples from different moments in Roman history.

rubric.label: Reasoning
rubric.description: Explains how the evidence supports the comparison rather than listing events.

rubric.label: Complication
rubric.description: Addresses a limit, exception, or interaction between size and political conflict.

rubric.label: Accuracy
rubric.description: Keeps the chronology and the distinction between western and eastern Rome clear.

review.front: Why does Roman imperial history continue after 476 CE?
